title: LOOK BACK: Bea Millan-Windorski’s Miss Universe 2026 journey
summary: From her strong pre-pageant performances to her third-place finish, the Filipina bet from La Union centered her Miss Universe campaign on Filipino culture and environmental advocacy

blocks.text: Bea Millan-Windorski capped her Miss Universe campaign with a third runner-up finish at the 75th edition of the pageant in Puerto Rico on Wednesday, November 25 (Manila time), after a strong run right from the preliminary events.

Windorski was among the first delegates to arrive in Puerto Rico on November 8. At the November 11 welcome parade in Aguadilla, she wore a fringed blue ensemble by Filipino designer Anthony Ramirez, inspired by the shared music, dance, and island cultures of the Philippines and the Caribbean. She also completed her closed-door interview ahead of the preliminary competition.

The 24-year-old Filipino-American model, writer, and consultant for climate and social impact organizations wore “Diwa ng Kordilyera,” also designed by Ramirez, during the national costume show on November 22 (Manila time).

The ensemble combined Kalinga-inspired tattoo patterns, beadwork and Mountain Province weaving with stacked earthen vessels inspired by the Kalinga Banga Salidsid, which pays tribute to Kalinga women who traditionally carried water along steep mountain paths and rice terraces.

In an interview, Windorski said she was proud to represent the Kalinga people. She said the costume honored the women’s resilience and sought to “raise awareness of clean water access for remote communities.”
She also discussed Kalinga’s history of resisting colonization and the importance of protecting indigenous communities and natural resources.

During the preliminary competition on November 23, Windorski introduced herself as “Filipinas,” drawing cheers from the crowd. She wore a blue two-piece swimsuit by Rian Fernandez Atelier with a flowing cape inspired by the waves of La Union.

For the evening gown, she wore “The Golden Seas of Sulu,” an Anthony Ramirez creation with gold embellishments that pay tribute to Mindanao’s gold craftsmanship, and blue details that represent the Sulu Sea.

Ahead of the finals, Windorski reunited with her parents in Puerto Rico and shared a Jaggy Glarino look celebrating T’boli beadwork from South Cotabato. The contemporary outfit paired the beadwork with exaggerated butterfly sleeves.

In her post, she said she wanted to wear something that reminded her of the country she was representing and its artistry. She added that she was proud to carry “a little piece” of the Philippines with her.

Windorski advanced to the Top 30 and then the Top 12 after the swimsuit round. For the evening gown competition, she wore “Pearl of the Orient,” another Anthony Ramirez creation inspired by Cebu’s white-sand shores and the Philippines’ nickname as the “Pearl of the Orient.”

The gown featured mother-of-pearl seashell, coral and pawikan motifs, plus a sun motif inspired by the Philippine flag. She said white also honored her mother’s dream of seeing her win in a white dress and the white gown worn by her favorite Miss Universe in Puerto Rico.
After reaching the Top 5, she was asked how she would convince people that the pageant remained relevant after 75 years.
Windorski said the prestigious pageant honors women’s past, present and future, and pledged to work with the United Nations for climate-displaced communities and vulnerable voices.

For the final question, she was asked what the world needed most from its leaders. Drawing on a decade of sea turtle volunteering, she described how stronger hatchlings help weaker nestmates reach the sea. She called it “turtle mentality” and urged leaders to embrace the same spirit of cooperation, saying, “When one rises, we all rise.”
Windorski was crowned Miss Universe Philippines 2026 on May 2, where she competed as the delegate of La Union.

During the pageant, she was asked why the Philippines remained worth representing despite public frustration with the country. She cited the “limitless potential of the Filipino people” and called for more local opportunities so Filipinos would not have to leave their families to “survive and thrive.”
Windorsk previously represented the United States at Miss Earth 2024, where she won the Miss Earth-Water title.

Her grandparents Alfredo and Marcela Millan originally lived in San Juan, La Union, before moving to Nueva Vizcaya. They later immigrated to the United States, where her mother met her American father, whose family has Polish and German immigrant roots.

Raised in Milwaukee, Millan-Windorski regularly visited La Union, where she developed a connection to the province and its environmental causes, including sea turtle conservation and disaster response. She later drew inspiration from local conservation group Project CURMA and, in 2025, joined the Environmentalists Against Corruption Alliance. – Rappler.com
Dominique Astucia is a Rappler intern studying BA Journalism at the University of Santo Tomas.
